extraction.teacher_style: The teacher provides clear, step-by-step instructions with a focus on both footwork and upper-body synchronization. She uses a supportive and encouraging tone, often incorporating her dance partner to demonstrate the social aspect of the dance.

lesson_structure.note: Adding shoulder movements to the footwork.
Demonstration of a modified, shorter step.

metaphors: the top doesn't know what the bottom is doing
common_mistakes: crossing the foot from the back instead of the front
stiffening the arms while holding hands
safety: be aware of rings that can pinch your partner's hand
don't rub against your partner if wearing sequins to avoid skin irritation

steps_taught.name: 3-step
steps_taught.description: A sequence of taps and a cross-step.

what_works: breaking down complex movements into smaller parts
what_hinders: the teacher's movements are sometimes obscured by her clothing

quotes.text: Sometimes this is the harder part.
Sometimes this is the hardest for people.
And it's okay to mess up, you can just continue.
Don't start your own khigga, just follow one khigga all the way around.
Don't stiffen up, because your partner will have to like forcibly try to dance with you.

evidence_segments.observation: The teacher demonstrates the basic footwork by tapping and crossing her feet.
The teacher demonstrates the shoulder movement by lifting and lowering them in a rhythmic pattern.
The teacher introduces her partner and explains the social aspect of the dance.
The teacher and her partner perform the basic 3-step dance together while holding hands.
The teacher demonstrates a modified, shorter version of the step.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher emphasizes the social etiquette of the dance, such as how to join a line and how to handle physical contact with partners.
